name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Dorea; g__Dorea_A is one of those parts and its genomes are labelled Dorea in NCBI.

sentences.text: Dorea members are Gram-positive, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming rods isolated from human faeces and belonging to the Clostridium coccoides rRNA group.
The genus was established when Eubacterium formicigenerans was reclassified, with Dorea longicatena described at the same time.
One gut Dorea strain transforms primary bile acids in two steps into 3-alpha and 3-beta secondary bile acids.
Another human faecal Dorea strain cleaves carbon-linked glycosides, converting the isoflavone puerarin to daidzein.
